title: Weakness and Grace
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: Weakness and grace teaches that human limitation, frailty, and inability can become places where God displays His sufficient grace and power. Weakness does not disqualify believers from God’s care or usefulness.
summary: Weakness and grace teaches that human limitation, frailty, and inability can become places where God displays His sufficient grace and power. Weakness does not disqualify believers from God’s care or usefulness.
christFocus: Jesus Christ meets His people in weakness with sufficient grace. His power is made perfect not through human boasting, but through dependence on Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Scripture does not teach believers to despise weakness as worthless. Human weakness exposes the limits of self-reliance and creates space for dependence on God’s grace.

Paul learned that God’s grace was sufficient and that Christ’s power was made perfect in weakness. This does not make weakness pleasant, but it transforms how believers understand it.

Weakness may include physical limitation, emotional weariness, disability, grief, temptation, poverty, exhaustion, or inability to control outcomes. God is not ashamed to meet His people there.

The Gospel humbles human boasting. God often works through what the world considers weak so that His grace, not human strength, receives the glory.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people feel useless because they are weak. They may compare themselves to the strong, visible, gifted, or productive and assume God has little purpose for them. This doctrine says grace is sufficient in the very place they feel disqualified.

It also corrects pride in ministry. God’s work does not depend on impressive flesh. His power is displayed through dependent people who know they need Him.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Bring weakness to Christ instead of hiding it in shame or covering it with pride. Ask for grace, receive help, and serve from dependence rather than self-sufficiency. Encourage the weak as necessary members of the body, not burdens to be managed.
